headline: This 2014 law keeps certain trucking safety exemptions for home heating fuel deliveries in place until May 31, 2014, unless the Transportation Department ends the emergency sooner.
what_it_does: It applies to emergency exemptions from federal motor carrier safety rules that FMCSA issued or extended between February 5, 2014, and the day the law was signed. Those exemptions were meant to give relief to trucks directly delivering propane and home heating fuel. The law keeps them in effect until May 31, 2014, unless the Secretary of Transportation finds the emergency ended earlier. It does not stop FMCSA from issuing or extending exemptions past that date under other federal law.

who_it_affects.group: Commercial truck drivers delivering propane and home heating fuel
who_it_affects.how: They may operate under the covered exemptions from federal motor carrier safety rules until May 31, 2014, unless DOT ends the emergency sooner.

who_it_affects.group: Trucking companies that haul propane and home heating oil
who_it_affects.how: They can rely on the covered exemptions during the extended period instead of complying with the standard safety rules those exemptions relieve.

who_it_affects.group: Households that heat their homes with propane or heating oil
who_it_affects.how: The law aims to keep fuel deliveries moving during the emergency, but it does not change prices, delivery schedules, or payment programs.

when_it_takes_effect: The law took effect when it was signed on March 21, 2014. The covered exemptions remain in effect through May 31, 2014, unless DOT ends the emergency earlier.
